int_name: N AMERICAN ST & CECIL B MOORE AVE

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a very wide roadway with embedded rail tracks and faded crosswalk markings. While a sidewalk exists on one side, the lack of signals, signage, or refuge islands creates a high-exposure crossing for pedestrians in an industrial context.

hazards.name: Rail tracks in crossing
hazards.description: Embedded rail tracks create an uneven surface and tripping hazard for pedestrians within the marked crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway crossing the foreground

hazards.name: Excessive crossing distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway width increases pedestrian exposure time to vehicular traffic without any mid-point refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire width of the foreground roadway

hazards.name: Uncontrolled crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks any accompanying signage or signals to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised refuge island in the center of the roadway to reduce exposure and allow for two-stage crossing.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Repaint the faded crosswalk with high-visibility ladder or zebra patterns to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-activated flashing beacons to increase driver yielding rates at this uncontrolled crossing.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment includes basic infrastructure such as sidewalks and a marked crosswalk, but lacks formal traffic control at the intersection. A significant safety concern is the large trailer parked near the corner, which creates a major visual obstruction for both pedestrians and drivers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A large white trailer is parked immediately adjacent to the crosswalk, blocking sightlines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are significantly worn and faded, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs or traffic signals are visible to regulate the right-of-way at this intersection.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking and obstructions near the corner to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk using high-visibility thermoplastic markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position.

result.summary: The street features a wide, uncontrolled crossing with high-visibility zebra markings but lacks any signage or signals to alert drivers. Embedded rail tracks within the roadway present a significant tripping hazard and complicate the crossing for those with mobility aids or bicycles.

hazards.name: Embedded Rail Tracks
hazards.description: Rail tracks in the roadway can cause tripping or trap bicycle tires.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway crossing

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Wide Crossing
hazards.description: A long crossing distance across multiple lanes without a refuge island or signalization.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add user-actuated flashing lights to increase driver awareness and yielding at the crosswalk.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides, but lacks active traffic control such as signals or stop signs for the primary roadway. The wide crossing distance and potential sightline obstructions from overgrown vegetation on the corner increase risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Wide Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross a wide roadway with no visible traffic signals or stop signs to halt vehicle flow.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Overgrown vegetation on the right side of the intersection may block the view between drivers and pedestrians entering the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image near the corner

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-activated flashing lights to alert drivers to the presence of people in the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or remove overgrown bushes on the corner to clear sightlines for all road users.
